These five steps are: collation, then evaluation, which has to do with liability of the source, credibility of the information. This is followed by analysis and integration, which are almost conducted simultaneously. And at the end of the processing phase there is the integration or the so-called integration. And if you want, I can explain what these terms stand for, but it's basically a mental process whereby you review information in order to draw relevant conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That should actually be sufficient. You have already mentioned the reliability of sources. How do you determine whether a source is reliable and the information provided credible?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The criteria as being applied in the intelligence cycle also applied to any form of scientific research. To keep matters simple, one of the criteria you will look -- or you will consider is the distance -- I'm sorry, the relationship between the source and the information. And that relationship covers all aspects. It can be a purely -- I mean, factual aspect, i.e., the distance, the physical distance, was the source there or not, or is it -- is the source reporting information provided by somebody else. The time relationship can be of importance, whether the source provided information soon after the event or much later. Obviously, an important aspect is the reputation of the source; i.e., this applies specifically to open sources. Many open sources, I wouldn't call them biased, but they may be related to one or the other party who may have an interest in the events you are reporting on, and that relationship can influence the way in which that source reports the events. Now, in this context, as you can see from the report, I mean for the largest part, the sources I have consulted are what I would call primary sources, i.e., VRS, SRBiH, TO, and other -- or, JNA, SFRY armed forces military documentation, as well as SRBiH and followed by RS political or more civilian documents, primary sources whereby these organisations and structures report about their own activity. So there would be, I mean from a purely doctrinal point of view, a higher degree of reliability with these sources, but, of course, you will look also for other sources in order to check corroboration. And that brings us to the issue of credibility of the information. The fact that the same information or the same facts is reported several times does not add to the credibility of the information, but it can -- it can assist. What you will look for is the context. For example, when we see information for the first time and it doesn't fit into the context, we will conduct additional searches, again applying the same methodology, in order to try to -- in order to assess and establish the credibility of that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in relation to the review and analysis, what time-frame did the documentation cover that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: When we consider the two parts of the report, basically, it starts in the mid-1980s, specifically for relevant regulations applying to the SFRY armed forces consisting of JNA and TO, and it ends -- I think the last document I include is from November 1995. And for Part 2, obviously most of the documentation covers the time-period, say, from November 1991 to November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: As far as B/C/S documents were concerned, would you only work with the English translation or would you also look at the original versions of the document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would also look at the original version. I'm not a B/C/S speaker, but after all the years here, you become familiar with military terminology. And, for example, I would conduct searches on unit numbers. Each military unit has a military post number. When, for example -- I mean, as you see in the military orders and reports have a number, a reference number, well, that can also be a search criteria. There are standardised -- I mean, standard expressions that I used, I mean, directives, instructions, and so on, ordered. Names of towns, names of individuals, can all be used as search criteria, and that allows you to gather -- I mean, to collect more information that is relevant for the subject-matter of the report. And just to finalise the answer, I wouldn't just search on the English terms, but also look at the B/C/S terminology. And in case of doubt, I could rely on a language assistance in the Military Analysis Team who helped me out for that. I also had glossaries available to me so in order to make sure that I could conduct the most comprehensive searches possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your report includes a huge amount of references to documents. On which basis did you choose these particular documents?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, as I explained in the scope of methodology, I mean, based on the direction -- the direction was given by the senior trial attorney to write a report about a specific topic. I then try to understand what that implied. Obviously, I also relied on my previous experience here and reports I had drafted for related cases. And then I would apply the intelligence cycle, i.e., determine search criteria. And based on this -- I mean, this is a continuous process. So you have a search criteria. This will then also allow you to identify additional search criteria. And then again applying the intelligence cycle, I would accumulate information which I would organise depending on topics. I would create a draft table of contents for my report which would cover the main aspects I would like to cover, in report of which I consider relevant for the scope of the report. And, obviously, documents that I would have found and -- would generate again new search terms, and new searches, and so on, and this would be a continuous process then. And then I would, of course, apply the different criteria in order to establish whether a source I had was reliable and whether the information that was reported by that source was credible. And so I've tried to focus on primary sources because there were so many available, and as I mentioned, mainly documentation from SFRY armed forces, JNA, Bosnian Serb TO, VRS, as well as, obviously, documents from the political side, SFRY Presidency, SRBiH Presidency, RS Presidency, RS Supreme Command, and so on, as you can see in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did you author the entire report or did you incorporate the work of other analysts?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm the only author of this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And since writing the report, have you found any material which would change your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not about changing conclusions. But, for example, the addendum there, I conducted additional searches, and then I established whether these documents had any added value, and these documents allow to further specify certain conclusions. But there were no documents that made me change conclusions I included in Parts 1 and Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did you have an opportunity to review a consolidated report that incorporates the addendum and the corrigendum in the report you authored in April 2009?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 65 ter 11702 be brought up on the screen, and the first page is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you look at the date of this page, is that the consolidated report that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours, and "Consolidated" stands for incorporating all the parts of the report, including addendum and corrigendum.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And is this consolidated report an accurate amalgamation of the three documents? Did you check that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And while reviewing the report, did you identify two aspects that you wanted to clarify?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 60 of this report. No, that's not correct. I need 0704-6531, ERN number. It's further down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 60 on Part 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, page 60 on Part 2, yes. And it's actually starting at the bottom and continuing on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I quote here: "On 12 May 1992, the Assembly of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina elect Radovan Karadzic, Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic as the members of the Presidency of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On the same day, the members of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Presidency elect Radovan Karadzic to president of the SRBiH." Would you like to make a clarification here, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. It should read "President of the Presidency of the SRBiH."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that same error is also in the paragraph 35 of the executive summary of the report. And as we are at it, can we please have 65 ter 11001 on the screen. No, 11 -- 00111. Both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, looking at this document, is that the one you have referred to in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can this please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3032, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please again have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. It's 3032, and the previous one as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Can we please have again the Exhibit -- the consolidated report, 65 ter 11702, and now, please, in Part 2, page 178. It's not -- it's not correct. There should be a reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, I have this ERN number, but I'm looking for, actually, a reference to an alleged involvement of Serb forces in serious crime in Bosanski Samac. What is it here? It should --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it should be page 177.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, 177, so one earlier. Oh, sorry. 177, please, the one previous. Yes, correct. Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You were referred here -- you refer here to a case in the Military Court in Banja Luka, sentencing several persons to prison terms for crimes and, I quote: "... unlawful deprivation of liberty against a number of civilians in the village of Donji Sabari [phoen], Samac municipality, November 1992." Mr. Theunens, when you look at this decision, what did you find out in relation to the perpetrators and the victims of these particular incidents? Were they, as you say here, civilians or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I had the opportunity to review the source or the document I used, i.e., the judgement by the Banja Luka Military Court, and I stand corrected; that is, that the accused were members of the VRS, as well as the victims. So it shouldn't read "civilians" in this Roman numeral iv, but it should read "members of the VRS."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, with these two clarifications, I request the report, 65 ter 11702, in this consolidated form be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3033, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have up-loaded also a track changes version of that document, where one can easily see what is a correction, what is an addendum, and that is under 11702A. I don't know whether we also need to admit that or not. I would think yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's admit it. Exhibit P3034. And I note the time. It's time to rise for today.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume tomorrow at 9.00. Yes, we need to rise immediately. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of July, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
